keyVerseText: Josiah was eight years old when he began to reign, and he reigned thirty and one years in Jerusalem. And his mother's name was Jedidah, the daughter of Adaiah of Boscath.
rootMeaning: The root of יְדִידָה (Yᵉdîydâh) is יְדִיד (yᵉdîyd), which conveys the idea of being beloved or amiable. As a feminine noun derived from this root, יְדִידָה literally means "beloved woman" or "lovely one." This etymology enriches the common English gloss by emphasizing not only affection but also a sense of cherished endearment, highlighting relational warmth and value beyond a simple name.
usageInScripture: יְדִידָה appears only once in the entire Scripture, specifically as a proper name for the mother of King Josiah in 2 Kings 22:1. The translation consistently renders her name as Jedidah, reflecting her identity as the "beloved" woman in the royal lineage. This singular occurrence underscores the personal and historical significance of the name, rather than a general descriptive term, anchoring it firmly in a biographical context.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding יְדִידָה as "beloved" enriches our grasp of biblical personhood, showing how names often carry profound meaning tied to character or divine favor. As the mother of Josiah, a king noted for his covenant renewal and reform, Jedidah's name may symbolize the cherished role of godly lineage and maternal influence in God's redemptive plan. This reminds believers that God values and endears individuals within His sovereign purposes, highlighting the intimate relationship between God and His people. Such a name invites reflection on how believers are beloved by God, called to live in faithfulness as part of His covenant family.
keyVerseReflection: 2 Kings 22:1 notes that Josiah began to reign at eight years old, and his mother was named Jedidah, the daughter of Adaiah. The inclusion of her name, meaning "beloved," adds depth to the verse by highlighting the personal and familial context behind Josiah's kingship. It suggests that Josiah's godly reign was rooted not only in royal succession but also in the nurturing and beloved heritage represented by his mother, underscoring the providential care behind his leadership in Jerusalem.
